property_summary: pastBlockTime strictly increases after any call to fallback, regardless of whether the balance transfer happens.
If the fallback function transfers ether, the state variable pastBlockTime must have been updated.
After a call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether, the state variable pastBlockTime is always set to the current block.timestamp.
After calling fallback with any value, the contract's pastBlockTime should be strictly greater than zero or equal to zero only if the call reverted.
Sending exactly 10 ether to the fallback function within the same timestamp as a previous successful call always reverts.
When sending exactly 10 ether to the fallback function, the call must always succeed and update pastBlockTime to a value greater than the previous value.
When calling fallback with 10 ether and a timestamp greater than pastBlockTime, the call succeeds; with any other value it reverts.
The fallback function reverts when block.timestamp equals pastBlockTime, ensuring strictly increasing timestamps.
After sending exactly 10 ether, the contract's balance should be zero if and only if the block number is a multiple of 15.
After sending exactly 10 ether at a later timestamp, the contract's balance decreases only if block.number % 15 satisfies the condition in the original contract.
When sending exactly 10 ether at a strictly increasing timestamp, if the contract receives a call on a block number not divisible by 15, it should not transfer its entire balance.
The contract balance after a successful fallback call that triggers the transfer should be zero in the reference and non-zero in the mutant.
After a fallback call that triggers the if-block (block.number % 15 == 0), the contract balance decreases by exactly the sent amount (the contract's full balance in reference, 1 ether in mutant).
After a sequence of two fallback calls, the contract balance either returns to zero (reference) or remains positive (mutant), depending on block heights.

After a successful fallback call that satisfies the transfer condition (block.number % 15 == 0), the contract balance changes by exactly the amount sent, which is the full balance in the reference and 1 ether in the mutant.

After a successful fallback call (msg.value == 10 ether, block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) that also triggers the if-block (block.number % 15 == 0), the contract's ether balance must decrease by exactly the contract's full balance before the call, not by a fixed 1 ether.
